title: Console Simulated Traffic Runner — Release Notes 1.0
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Overview:

This document contains the release notes for Console Simulated Traffic Runner (STR) v1.0 — a developer-facing, browser-integrated tool for producing realistic, configurable synthetic traffic against Redwood inference routes from the Console. STR v1.0 is intended to accelerate on-boarding, load-testing, and fidelity regression experiments without requiring customers to run external traffic generators.

Key goals for 1.0:
- Provide a lightweight, zero-install traffic simulator embedded in Console for rapid developer experiments.
- Support representative traffic shapes: conversational sessions, bursty transactional requests, batched embedding requests, and long-generation streams.
- Emit telemetry compatible with production consumption metrics so experiments mirror billing and SLO signals.
- Offer safe modes (read-only, cost caps) to prevent runaway charges in self-serve accounts.

Change summary (what's new):
- Console UI: New "Simulate Traffic" tab on Route detail pages with pre-built scenarios and a configurable scenario editor.
- Scenario library: 12 curated scenarios (e.g., ─ low-latency chat, high-throughput batching, heavy-KV eviction, streaming long-context) plus the ability to define custom sequences.
- Execution engine: In-Console runner that executes HTTP/SDK-compatible requests against the selected route with control over concurrency, arrival distribution (poisson, fixed, burst), and sequence length.
- Cost & SLO preview: Each scenario shows estimated token cost, projected p50/p95 latency impact, and error-rate delta based on historical baseline.
- Telemetry integration: STR streams experiment telemetry to the same ingestion pipeline as production, tagged with experiment_id. Telemetry includes per-request timing, token counts, retry events, fallback occurrences, and model-variant selection.
- Safety controls: Per-experiment budget caps, per-account max concurrency defaults, and an optional confirmation step for any scenario that could exceed a configured monthly cost threshold.

Why this matters:
- Engineers can validate performance and fidelity trade-offs early in feature development without needing a separate load-test environment.
- Product and SRE teams gain consistent signals from experiments because measurements use production-grade telemetry and cost models.
- Sales and Customer Success can demonstrate predictable migration scenarios to Dedicated and Private customers during onboarding.

Supported platforms and limits in 1.0:
- Availability: Hosted Console only (Global region). Private Deployment support is planned for 2.0.
- Max concurrent virtual clients per experiment: 200.
- Max sustained request rate per route from STR: 1,200 rps (soft limit; subject to route quota).
- Max scenario length (in tokens generated per session): 8,192 tokens.

Configuration reference (table):
- name: scenario_name — (string) human-friendly label.
- arrival_pattern: poisson|fixed|burst — (string) selects arrival distribution.
- concurrency: (integer) simulated parallel clients.
- payload_template: (string) templated request body supporting variables ({{user_id}}, {{seed_prompt}}).
- token_budget: (integer) cap on tokens for experiment (safety).
- model_variant: (string) explicit variant OR leave blank for routing policy.
- duration_seconds: (integer) duration of the run.

Quickstart (Console):
1) Navigate to Console → Routes → <your-route> → Simulate Traffic.
2) Choose a curated scenario (e.g., "Chat: bursty onboarding") or Create New.
3) Adjust concurrency and token_budget. If you exceed your default budget cap, the Run button will be greyed out until you acknowledge the cost.
4) Click Run and observe live telemetry in the experiment panel.

CLI (beta) example (curl):
- The Console exposes a one-time experiment token for CLI-driven orchestration (intended for CI integration). Example:
  1) Request an experiment token from Console (POST /api/console/experiments/token)
  2) Run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/experiments/run -H 'Authorization: Bearer <EXPERIMENT_TOKEN>' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","scenario":"chat-burst","concurrency":50,"duration_seconds":300}'

Telemetry and cost alignment:
- STR uses the same tokenization and cost model as production billing. Experiment telemetry includes experiment_id and scenario_name tags so team owners can aggregate cost and latency impacts in dashboards.
- Experiment events are sampled by default at 100% for the experiment lifecycle and retained for 7 days in product tiers; longer retention is available via Optimize add-on.

SLO & safety interactions:
- Running STR does not modify production route quotas but will be subject to rate-limiting if a route is under global contention. STR will gracefully back off and report fallback events.
- STR supports a "canary" target option: tagged requests that are routed to a variant pool (canary) so teams can validate variants without impacting the main fleet.

Upgrade/migration notes for existing teams:
- No config changes required to routes. STR calls the route endpoints exactly as a customer client would; existing access controls (API keys, per-route tokens) are used.
- Admins can disable STR per account from Console → Settings → Experimentation to prevent usage in regulated tenants.

Rollout and availability timeline:
- 2026-09-15: Internal beta (Redwood employees + select partners).
- 2026-09-29: Early access for self-serve accounts.
- 2026-10-01: Public launch (GA) — feature enabled by default for all hosted accounts.

Owners and contacts:
- Product owner: Sofia Chen (product) — sofia.chen@redwood.ai
- Engineering: Marco Ruiz (eng-platform) — @mruiz
- SRE & telemetry: Jamie Patel (eng-sre) — @jpatel

SDK and API compatibility notes:
- STR issues requests using the same REST/SDK surface as documented for hosted inference. If the route supports function/tool-calling and streaming, STR can simulate both.
- For streaming scenarios, STR simulates slow and fast producers to reproduce partial-response conditions.

Known limitations and caveats:
1) Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) are not supported in 1.0. Do not rely on STR measurements for air-gapped performance planning.
2) STR executes experiments from Console-hosted agents; cross-region latency skew may affect measurements for routes pinned to a specific region. Document observed region offset in experiment notes.
3) Very high-fidelity fidelity regressions that depend on customer data integrations (e.g., embeddings backed by customer-owned vector DB) will be approximate unless the customer integrates the data into the scenario template.
4) Cost-estimates are conservative projections based on the last 30d median token size; actual billing may vary for dynamic or multi-model routing policies.

Troubleshooting (common issues):
- Experiment stalls at "Initializing": check that the route has a valid active model and that the account has remaining token budget.
- Observed fallback spikes: examine the experiment timeline for rate-limit or variant-fallback tags; reduce concurrency or switch to canary variant pools.
- Telemetry not visible in dashboards: confirm experiment_id tag inclusion and that the account's telemetry ingestion is enabled. Contact SRE if missing events are systemic.

Security and compliance:
- All simulated requests are stamped with an experiment tag to prevent accidental ingestion into customer logs and to mark any resulting outputs as non-production in downstream pipelines.
- Experiment tokens are single-use and short-lived (default TTL: 10 minutes).
- Admins can configure retention and disable experiment telemetry at account level for regulated customers.

Documentation and training resources:
- In-Console guided tour (Simulate Traffic → Tour).
- Workshop: "Using STR to size Dedicated capacity" — hands-on lab content in Learn Portal (internal).
- API reference: Console Experiment API (internal link).

Feedback and next steps (planned improvements):
- Private Deployment agent for on-prem performance parity (v2.0).
- Scenario provenance: recording seed prompts and deterministic replay for fidelity reproduction (v1.2).
- Integration with Optimize to automatically suggest batching and quantization settings from experiment results (v1.3).

Appendix: experiment JSON example
{
  "scenario_name": "chat-burst-onboarding",
  "arrival_pattern": "burst",
  "concurrency": 75,
  "duration_seconds": 180,
  "payload_template": "{\"input\": \"Hello, I need help onboarding\"}"
}

If you find issues or need higher-capacity trials for enterprise demo, contact the product owner or join #console-sim-runner on Slack.

Changelog:
- 2026-09-15 — v1.0 initial GA (S. Chen): Public launch and documentation published.
- 2026-10-01 — v1.0.1 (S. Chen): Adjusted cost estimation algorithm to include variant routing overhead in estimates.
